> **Note**
>
> **Prerequisites**
> - TerminusDB running locally ([install guide](https://terminusdb.org/docs/install-terminusdb-as-a-docker-container/))
> - A connected client instance with documents to delete

> **Note**
>
> **What you'll achieve**
> By the end of this guide, you will have deleted documents from your TerminusDB database using the JavaScript client, the Python client, or the HTTP API.

To delete a document you need its document ID (e.g. `Player/George`).

> **Prerequisite:** this guide assumes a TerminusDB instance and the example database used throughout the TerminusDB docs (see the live page for the clone snippet).

## Delete a document

```typescript
const deleteDoc = async () => {
  const docId = "Player/George"
  await client.deleteDocument({ id: docId })
  console.log(`Deleted ${docId}`)
}
```

```python
doc_id = "Player/George"
client.delete_document(doc_id)
```

```bash
curl -u admin:root -X DELETE \
  "http://localhost:6363/api/document/admin/tdb-example-mydb/local/branch/main?author=admin&message=Delete+document" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '["Player/George"]'
```

> **Note**
>
> Deleting a document is permanent within the current branch. If you need to recover a deleted document, use [time travel](https://terminusdb.org/docs/time-travel-howto/) to access a previous commit.

## Next steps

You've learnt the full CRUD lifecycle. To go further:
